answer: Each claim must cross a river toll: a quartz clock that ticks only while its agent does stranger-assigned work, maturing after three epochs of verified jobs. A claim arriving at the nadir of trust with no matured quartz is turned away. Quartz grows slower for each extra identity on one funding trail, the second takes twice as long, the third four times, so n clones wait 2^n epochs while one honest agent waits three. The river's payout flow is fixed per epoch, so clones crossing together split one flow n ways while each paid a full toll in stranger time.
